misconceptions.statement: Solar panels work by trapping the Sun's heat to boil water and turn turbines.
misconceptions.why: Students link solar with heat from the Sun and with steam turbines in thermal plants.
misconceptions.fix: Solar photovoltaic cells directly change light into electricity without heat or moving parts. Only solar thermal systems use heat.

probe.question: How does a solar panel on a roof make electricity?
probe.wrong_answer: It heats water to steam which spins a turbine.

misconceptions.root_belief: all electricity comes from spinning turbines

misconceptions.statement: Solar panels need hot weather and give no electricity in cool weather.
misconceptions.why: Students mix up heat with light because the Sun gives both.
misconceptions.fix: Solar cells use light, not heat, and actually work slightly better when cool. Bright sunny winter days give good output.

probe.question: Will a solar panel work well on a bright, cold day in Leh?
probe.wrong_answer: No, it is too cold for solar panels.

misconceptions.root_belief: heat and light are the same thing

misconceptions.statement: Solar parks take away land only from forests, so they are always harmful to nature.
misconceptions.why: Large land use is easily linked with cutting forests.
misconceptions.fix: Many Indian solar parks are built on barren or dry land such as Bhadla in Rajasthan, though land use must still be planned carefully.

probe.question: On what kind of land are many large Indian solar parks built?
probe.wrong_answer: Cleared forest land.

misconceptions.root_belief: one example represents all cases

misconceptions.statement: Rooftop solar panels store the electricity for use only on that house and can never send power to the grid.
misconceptions.why: Students picture the panel as a self-contained battery.
misconceptions.fix: Many rooftop systems are connected to the grid and send extra electricity to it (net metering), and the household gets credit.

probe.question: A house makes more solar power than it needs at noon. What can happen to the extra?
probe.wrong_answer: It is wasted because it cannot leave the house.

misconceptions.root_belief: what you cannot see does not exist

misconceptions.statement: A rooftop solar system gives power at night if it is a good panel.
misconceptions.why: Students think panels hold energy like a battery.
misconceptions.fix: Panels make electricity only when light falls on them. Night supply needs a battery or the grid.

probe.question: A home has rooftop panels and no battery. Does it get solar power at 9 pm?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, the panels keep supplying it.

misconceptions.root_belief: a device stores what it produces

misconceptions.statement: Wind turbines make wind by spinning their blades.
misconceptions.why: Turbines look like big fans, and fans make wind.
misconceptions.fix: Wind turns the blades, and the spinning generator makes electricity. A turbine takes energy from wind; it does not create it.

probe.question: What makes the blades of a wind turbine rotate?
probe.wrong_answer: A motor inside spins them to make wind.

misconceptions.root_belief: things that look alike work the same way
misconceptions.source_hint: Studies of student ideas on energy transfer and appearance-based reasoning

misconceptions.statement: A wind farm can be built anywhere in India and give the same power.
misconceptions.why: Students forget wind speed differs by place.
misconceptions.fix: Wind farms need places with strong, steady winds, like Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and Rajasthan. Weak-wind places give little power.

probe.question: Which is a better spot for a wind farm: a windy coastal plateau or a sheltered valley?
probe.wrong_answer: Both are equally good.

misconceptions.root_belief: conditions are the same everywhere

misconceptions.statement: Renewable energy means the energy can be used again and again, like recycling.
misconceptions.why: The word renewable is mixed up with reuse or recycling.
misconceptions.fix: Renewable sources like sunlight and wind are naturally refilled, so they do not run out in human time. Energy used is not reused.

probe.question: Why is solar energy called renewable?
probe.wrong_answer: Because the same energy can be reused after it is used.

misconceptions.root_belief: a word means its everyday meaning
misconceptions.source_hint: Research on student understanding of energy resources and conservation vs. renewal

misconceptions.statement: Coal and petrol will be renewed quickly by nature if we wait a few years.
misconceptions.why: Students do not grasp geological time.
misconceptions.fix: Fossil fuels took millions of years to form, so on human timescales they are non-renewable and finite.

probe.question: If we use up coal, will nature replace it within a few decades?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, new coal forms quickly underground.

misconceptions.root_belief: natural processes are fast enough to notice

misconceptions.statement: Renewable energy causes no pollution or damage of any kind.
misconceptions.why: It is advertised as clean energy, and students hear only the good side.
misconceptions.fix: Renewables emit very little greenhouse gas while running, but making panels and turbines, mining materials, using land, and disposing of old panels have impacts.

probe.question: Does a solar park have any environmental impact?
probe.wrong_answer: No, it has no impact at all.

misconceptions.root_belief: clean means completely harmless

misconceptions.statement: Wind turbines cause global warming by stirring the air.
misconceptions.why: Students link big machines with changes in weather.
misconceptions.fix: Wind turbines do not release greenhouse gases while working, and they help reduce global warming by replacing fossil fuels.

probe.question: Do wind farms add greenhouse gases to the air while generating power?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, they warm the air by stirring it.

misconceptions.root_belief: big visible machines must change the climate

misconceptions.statement: India's 500 GW target means 500 GW of solar panels only.
misconceptions.why: Solar is the most talked-about renewable source.
misconceptions.fix: The target is 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030, which includes solar, wind, hydro, bio-energy and nuclear.

probe.question: What does India's 2030 target of 500 GW include?
probe.wrong_answer: Only solar panels.

misconceptions.root_belief: the best-known example is the whole category

misconceptions.statement: If India has 100 GW of solar capacity, it gets 100 GW of power all day and night.
misconceptions.why: Students treat installed capacity as constant output.
misconceptions.fix: Capacity is the maximum output. Solar plants produce that only in full sunshine, so the actual average output is much lower (roughly 20 to 25 percent for solar).

probe.question: A 10 MW solar plant runs for 24 hours. Does it give 240 MWh?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, 10 MW × 24 h = 240 MWh.

misconceptions.root_belief: maximum value is the usual value
misconceptions.source_hint: Research on student difficulties distinguishing power and energy

misconceptions.statement: Since solar and wind capacity is growing, India already gets most of its electricity from renewables.
misconceptions.why: News highlights rising capacity and records, hiding the share of actual generation.
misconceptions.fix: Coal still produces the majority of India's electricity, though renewables' share is rising fast.

probe.question: Which source supplies most of India's electricity today?
probe.wrong_answer: Solar and wind.

misconceptions.root_belief: news about growth means it is now dominant

misconceptions.statement: The International Solar Alliance is a company that sells solar panels.
misconceptions.why: The word alliance is unfamiliar and solar suggests business.
misconceptions.fix: The International Solar Alliance is a group of countries, started by India and France, to promote solar energy. It is not a company.

probe.question: What is the International Solar Alliance?
probe.wrong_answer: A company that makes solar panels.

misconceptions.root_belief: a name with a product word is a business

misconceptions.statement: Hydropower is a new kind of energy that India has only just started using.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse new focus on solar with newness of all renewables.
misconceptions.fix: Hydropower is one of the oldest renewable sources and India has used dams for electricity for over a century.

probe.question: Which renewable source has India used for the longest time for electricity?
probe.wrong_answer: Solar power.

misconceptions.root_belief: new in the news means new in time

misconceptions.statement: Solar panels give no power on cloudy days.
misconceptions.why: Students think of sunshine as all or nothing.
misconceptions.fix: Under clouds panels still work using scattered light, but make less power than in direct sun.

probe.question: On a cloudy afternoon, how much electricity does a solar panel make?
probe.wrong_answer: None at all.

misconceptions.root_belief: partial means none

misconceptions.statement: Because the Sun shines in India every day, solar power is always available and never needs backup.
misconceptions.why: Students notice the daytime Sun but forget night, clouds and seasons.
misconceptions.fix: Solar is available only in daytime and varies with clouds and seasons, so the grid needs storage or other sources at night.

probe.question: Can India run only on solar power with no storage?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because the Sun shines every day.

misconceptions.root_belief: what is usually true is always true

misconceptions.statement: Wind turbines keep making full power in calm weather because they are heavy and keep spinning.
misconceptions.why: Students think the momentum of heavy blades supplies energy.
misconceptions.fix: Without wind the blades stop and no electricity is made. Output also changes with wind speed.

probe.question: What happens to a wind turbine's output when the wind drops to near zero?
probe.wrong_answer: It stays the same because the blades are heavy.

misconceptions.root_belief: moving objects keep supplying energy forever

misconceptions.statement: Stronger wind always gives much more power until the turbine breaks, so more wind is always better.
misconceptions.why: Students assume more input means more output without limits.
misconceptions.fix: Power rises with wind speed up to a rated speed, then stays steady, and turbines shut down in very high winds for safety.

probe.question: In a storm with extremely high winds, what does a turbine do?
probe.wrong_answer: It makes the most power possible.

misconceptions.root_belief: bigger or more means more effect

misconceptions.statement: Batteries create new electricity from nothing, so storage makes extra energy.
misconceptions.why: Students think of a battery as a source.
misconceptions.fix: A battery stores energy that was made earlier, and some energy is lost, so it never gives more than what was put in.

probe.question: If you store 100 units in a battery, can you get back more than 100?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, a battery makes extra electricity.

misconceptions.root_belief: a device that gives energy also makes it
misconceptions.source_hint: Research on energy conservation and the idea of energy being produced

misconceptions.statement: Intermittency is a fatal flaw, so renewables can never supply a large share of electricity.
misconceptions.why: Students notice the problem but not the solutions.
misconceptions.fix: Using solar, wind, hydro, batteries and a connected grid together balances supply. Several countries already get large shares from renewables.

probe.question: Can a grid with a lot of solar and wind be reliable?
probe.wrong_answer: No, it cannot work at all.

misconceptions.root_belief: one problem makes the whole idea impossible

misconceptions.statement: Electric vehicles are completely pollution-free.
misconceptions.why: No smoke comes from the exhaust, so students assume no pollution exists.
misconceptions.fix: EVs have no exhaust, but electricity and battery manufacturing can cause emissions, especially if the power comes from coal.

probe.question: Does charging an EV from a coal-powered grid cause any pollution?
probe.wrong_answer: No, EVs never cause pollution.

misconceptions.root_belief: what you cannot see does not exist

misconceptions.statement: An electric vehicle has an engine that burns a special fuel.
misconceptions.why: Students picture all vehicles with an engine and a fuel tank.
misconceptions.fix: An EV has a battery that powers an electric motor. No fuel is burned in it.

probe.question: What makes the wheels of an electric car turn?
probe.wrong_answer: An engine burning a clean fuel.

misconceptions.root_belief: a rule from familiar cases works everywhere

misconceptions.statement: Switching to electric vehicles alone solves India's air pollution and carbon emissions.
misconceptions.why: Students think of a single cause and a single fix.
misconceptions.fix: EVs cut tailpipe pollution, but India's total emissions also come from coal power, industry, and farming, so cleaner electricity is needed too.

probe.question: If every car in India became electric but electricity stayed coal-based, would emissions fall to zero?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, all pollution would stop.

misconceptions.root_belief: one event has one single cause
